content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will officially launch for all users on Monday, September 14.

In addition, the company also stated that two features originally in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be introduced to iPhone users in a future software update, including the suggested features in Messages and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that these two features have been temporarily removed from iOS 27. The relevant changes also apply to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users earlier noticed that the automatic password changing feature had been removed from iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm this change.

In short, the suggested features in the Messages app can add information to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with one click based on the content of the user's conversation.

The following is Apple's description of the Passwords feature:

The Passwords app will attempt to go directly to websites where users use weak passwords or passwords that have been leaked, and automatically update the passwords. At WWDC, Apple explained that this feature will use Apple Intelligence and Safari to "take actions on behalf of the user in a proxy-like manner".

There are currently no further details on when these two features will be reintroduced in iOS 27. Apple's website simply states that the relevant features will be provided in a "future software update".
